rv.q: The three parts do not seem contemporary nor particularly enlightening about the female condition but they are curios and certainly show Wesker's compassion for, and insight into, working-class women.
McAuliffe weaves a fascinating evening of character work.
This is a production that truly “revisits” its text and makes it relevant to now.

cn.t: McAuliffe's updated revival of Wesker's 1981 monologue triptych earns mixed-to-positive reviews, with critics divided on its contemporary relevance but generally appreciating the intimate portraits of three women across different ages.
